title: Pay for funerals and dance jobs, and what he earned
summary: Funeral bands play free; Lawrence earned $2.50 when starting and $7-8 later, spending more on music than he made.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you think people spend more money on burial land than they used to? Oh yeah, yeah. They spend a lot more money, but not on music. Huh?

Not on music, no. Just on the other part, huh? Well the music, you know, it's kind of money for them. They're always free, you know, the bands are always free. They're never to charge for the music for a funeral anyway. They were always free.
Well it's cheap in New Orleans, you know, it's, was it 660 a man? There's union scale for a funeral.
To play for a parade? Yeah, that's not much.
No, it's not. Where some of those guys drink, they end up losing money.

Well some of them I guess they do it for the pleasure to get out of it. Not for the money because, I know if they had to play a parade and they have to have a job, they'll pay them better to work than to play the parade. But they just like it. You know, when you like something, you spend money to get that place.
A lot of them like to parade, grow the place. Yeah.

I know, I know, I spend more money playing music than making money. Is that right? Oh yeah. I used to leave, I had a shop, I had four men's work in the shop. Auto mechanical shop. And I used to leave here on Saturday and come back Monday. And at that time you wouldn't get too much money to play. It's $7, $8. Well I could make, I would stay here on Saturday evening and make as much as I could make, playing at night, but I just liked it.
What about when you were just starting, how much did you make?

Two and a half. Two and a half? Two dollars and a half. Well that's a good money. They used to give you a supper, two suppers, when you were good to the place, to eat supper and midnight they'd give you supper. Never had a good price at that time. That's good money for those days, you could buy a lot for two and a half.
